title: recovery-validation-suite: automated restore & failover validation for onprem/vpc
author: Aisha Choudhury
description: Motivation: recurring manual restore and failover exercises are slow, error-prone and hard to audit for private deployments (VPC and bare-metal). This PR introduces an opinionated recovery-validation suite (runbook-as-code + test harness) that automates snapshot restore, cross-AZ failover validation, and rollback checks. What this changes: 1) terraform/modules/recovery: new module to import/validate snapshots and produce a recoverable plan for both AWS VPC and Metal3 on-prem layouts; 2) helm/charts/recovery-validator: a small chart that runs staged recovery jobs as Kubernetes Jobs with idempotent hooks, preflight checks, and annotated runbook steps; 3) tooling: a CLI shim (scripts/recovery/rvctl) that sequences terraform apply/plan/destroy with a dry-run mode and integrates with the console audit events; 4) runbook-as-code: ansible/playbooks/recovery_playbook.yml and a collection of templated runbook steps in runbooks/recovery/ that can be executed or rendered as markdown for incident playbooks; 5) e2e: CI job definitions (ci/recovery-e2e.yml) to run a non-destructive smoke validation against test clusters and a destructive mode gated behind a flag. Checklist: - [x] terraform module for snapshot import & validation - [x] Helm chart with pre/post hooks and pod-level annotations for tracing - [x] rvctl shim for scripted runs and dry-run - [x] runbook templates and Ansible playbooks - [x] CI job + test harness + docs - [x] basic RBAC and KMS integration notes Included migrations/compatibility: the terraform module is opt-in (recovery_enabled = false by default). Backwards compatible with existing installer flows. Security: the module adds explicit KMS key bindings and requires least-privilege IAM roles for snapshot reads. Auditability: every automated run emits a structured event to the control-plane (console events endpoint) and stores run artifacts in a namespaced S3 prefix for postmortem and compliance. Risk: destructive validation is off by default and gated in CI. See linked Linear tickets for rollout plan.

Aisha: added annotation to skip PDB disruption checks and documented the destructive flag gating. (reply)
Marcus: CI failed on first run due to missing test credentials; re-ran and it passed. Please link the secure secret path in the CI docs. (approved after re-run)

release_notes: Adds an opt-in recovery validation suite for private deployments: new terraform recovery module, Helm recovery-validator chart, rvctl automation shim, Ansible runbook-as-code, and CI plumbing for non-destructive smoke tests. Destructive validations remain gated. See docs/private/recovery-validation.md for rollout steps and operator guidance.
